title: Code and data for: Partners, rivals, and friendly rivals in the evolution of direct reciprocity
description:
Code and data to reproduce every figure and table of the paper Partners, rivals, and friendly rivals in the evolution of direct reciprocity and its Supplementary Information.

A strategy of a repeated game is efficient if a population using it earns the largest average payoff any pair of players can attain, stable if it is a symmetric Nash equilibrium against a single deviant, and competitive if no co-player earns more than it does. The paper classifies all 16 binary memory-one and all 65536 binary memory-two strategies by these three properties at every symmetric two-player game, in the limit of rare errors. It then follows their evolution at 512 sampled games with a Wright-Fisher process with pairwise comparison.

The archive contains the following:

  • the exact census of the 65536 memory-two strategies, in C, in double precision and in exact rational arithmetic, with its check program;
  • the family descriptions of the friendly rivals;
  • the Fortran Wright-Fisher simulator in every version that ran on the cluster, with the seed of every replicate;
  • the reduced output of the census and of the simulations;
  • one folder per display item, with the Python script that redraws or recomputes it from the deposited data;
  • the notes on individual strategies and cycles to which the Supplementary Information refers, with the scripts that recompute their numbers.

The per-strategy abundance histograms of the memory-two runs are not included. They are regenerated bit for bit from the seeds, and simulator/CHECKSUMS.sha256 gives the sha256 of every packed output file to check a regeneration against.
